### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via mintPrincipalSession (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via organization_membership_ended (literal, a string literal in ApiKeyRefusalReason))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 49 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 49 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **50** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a0e29b844e4624c1f9d2c1afc307d4af231959c2` — the merge of head `bd20d79afb9f230473825ceb9baaac6d5f2581a3` into base `f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a0e29b844e4624c1f9d2c1afc307d4af231959c2 && git checkout a0e29b844e4624c1f9d2c1afc307d4af231959c2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420 bd20d79afb9f230473825ceb9baaac6d5f2581a3 && git checkout -B drift-repro f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420 && git merge --no-ff bd20d79afb9f230473825ceb9baaac6d5f2581a3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f18adce2f65b9de8ce3b7de1c3ba870bebb53420` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `15b303e0bfc3aaa636cded8c42e4e9171884c404`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts, packages/core/src/security/user-ban.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key-banned-owner.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/agent-forward-identity-view.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/principal-session-mint.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/api-key-banned-owner.dogfood.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts (and every runtime domain's `shouldDenyAnonymous` call), packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/types/src/driver-error-classification.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-ban-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json, better-auth 1.7.12 `packages/better-auth/src/plugins/admin/admin.ts` (the vendor sign-in hook the predicate mirrors), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-auth__src__agent-forward-identity-view.ts.json. Prose checked sentence by sentence in ③ only: .changeset/banned-user-credentials-refused.md, content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx, content/docs/permissions/administrator-guide.mdx.

Face: the committed changeset and the PR body both carry `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; `reviewFace` reads a `(narrowing)` arm on either value as the narrowing face, so this record is at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` and `--face declaration` does not apply. Read-only throughout: diff, PR body, head check-runs, cited code; no worktree, build, test or gate run.

Check-runs read on this head (two readings, the second at the end of the review): every completed run is `success` — Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped lints, Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Auto Label, filter. Still `in_progress` at the last reading: Test Core (8 shards), Test UI (16 shards), Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace. No red. The known main red (permission-set-clone-door dogfood) touches `permission-set-clone.ts` grants on `sys_comment` / `sys_activity`; nothing in this diff reaches that path, so it is not attributable here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set narrowing (the rule).** At the one key-admission seam (`resolveApiKeyAdmission`), after the key's own lifecycle verdict and before the tenancy and account-posture questions, the owner row is read by id as the system (`id`, `banned`, `ban_expires`) and a key whose owner's ban holds is answered on the `refused` arm with the new reason `owner_banned`: no principal, no fall-through to a session sent beside the key, nothing written (the use is not stamped). Verified in the tree: `hashApiKey` and the `sys_api_key` authentication read exist nowhere else at head (non-test, across packages/, ui/, examples/), so every door that resolves a key passes this check.
- **Wire answer per door** (judged from the cited code, not the PR's list): REST data door (`rest-server.ts`, `anonymous: 'fail-closed'`) — no principal ⇒ its anonymous 401, byte-identical to an unknown key, `WWW-Authenticate` included (dogfood pin compares all four fields). Runtime dispatcher, MCP HTTP door included (`resolve-execution-context.ts` ⇒ `resolveRequestExecutionContext`, per request) — every domain whose first statement is `shouldDenyAnonymous` answers the same 401 for both; `handleMcpRequest` refuses with one message for both. MCP stdio — refused at start ("did not resolve to a valid identity …", one generic sentence) and, for a live transport, on the next call (`resolvePrincipal` re-resolves per read; `initial` is reused for localization only). Storage family gate reader — acts only on `held`; the download door's identity comes from the shared composition, so a refused key resolves nobody there. service-print, service-datasource admin routes, cloud-connection, plugin-sharing — all through `resolveAuthzContext`, same empty context as an unknown key. Server-side the reason is one `warn` line (reason, key row id, owner id; never the key or hash).
- **Public surface widening.** `@objectstack/core` (root barrel re-exports `./security/index.js`) gains `isUserBanInForce`, `USER_BAN_FIELDS`, type `UserBanFields`; the published union `ApiKeyRefusalReason` gains the member `'owner_banned'` (an exhaustive consumer switch on that type will need the new arm — covered by the `yes` arm of the declaration). `ApiKeyAdmission` shape is unchanged.
- **plugin-auth's two existing ban checks now call the shared predicate.** `principal-session-mint.ts`: the flag is read in two further spellings (`'1'`, `'true'`) and a ban whose expiry equals the instant now still holds (previously lifted at equality) — one millisecond stricter, toward the vendor. `agent-forward-identity-view.ts`: the flag was read by truthiness and is now the closed set {true, 1, '1', 'true'}; equality at the instant now holds (previously lifted). Both rows arrive through the better-auth adapter as booleans, so the practical behaviour is unchanged; the direction of every change is toward the vendor's own rule. Both call sites keep their own refusal text.
- **Predicate parity with the vendor** (read at better-auth 1.7.12, `session.create.before`): flag set and no expiry ⇒ holds; expiry strictly past ⇒ lifts; expiry unreadable ⇒ holds. The predicate matches on each. Two deliberate differences the PR states correctly: it is read-only (the vendor clears a lapsed ban on the row; here a lapsed ban simply stops binding) and its flag test is a closed set rather than truthiness.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/banned-user-credentials-refused.md`: `@objectstack/core: patch`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start in both the changeset and the PR body; `**BREAKING**` banner; one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why. Level follows the Metadata-protocol kind alone: `none` ⇒ `patch` on both moved packages — correct. The body prescribes no code rewrite (the remedy is operational: lift the ban or mint a key under another user), so the `no-migration-prescription` category stands; `Check Changeset` and the repo/tooling lint lane that carries the ADR-0087 gate are green on this head.
- Packages moved by the diff: core and plugin-auth only; the dogfood package is private and takes no changeset. No spec change, no generated artefact, no `ui/` consumer of the changed exports (`git grep` of the three new names and of `isBanned` under `ui/` at head: none).
- ADR-0087 D3 obligations: nothing at rest changes, no authorable key moves, so no conversion or migration-chain entry is owed; the disposition says so in one line. ADR-0090 D10 rule 5 anchor on `agent-forward-identity-view.ts` (`scripts/adr-anchors/…`) still holds — the invariant "none for a banned or missing user" is implemented by the shared predicate, and the anchored ADR marker remains in the file header.

### ③ Boundary flags

PR-body open questions, each answered or escalated:
- *Revoked key answers `403 API_KEY_REVOKED` (distinguishable) while the banned owner's key matches the unknown key's `401`* — answered: the lifecycle arm is distinct by ruling A on the lifecycle card; the ban is an owner question and takes the generic answer, as the org-less refusal does. Correct ordering (lifecycle first) is read in the tree and pinned.
- *The inactivity window keeps running through a ban* — answered in the body; **prose flag (should-fix, see ④ item 3)**: the changeset's "Lifting the ban (or letting it expire) admits the same keys again, with nothing reissued" and `authentication.mdx`'s "restoring … its API keys" are unqualified; a key idle past the inactivity window during a long ban answers as inactive after the unban. One clause fixes both.
- *The ban flag is read whether or not the admin plugin is on* — true of the tree (the seam reads the row; nothing conditions on the plugin).
- *Whether a ban also revokes keys* — escalated as a maintainer question by the rule itself; the PR correctly does not decide it.
- *A key whose owner row is absent keeps today's answer* — stated in the body and pinned; **escalated** (④ item 2): now that the owner row is read on every admission, admitting a credential whose owner no longer exists is a choice the maintainer should make explicitly.
- Not raised by the PR, noted here as a boundary (not a finding): a banned user's non-credential execution paths (an automation `runAs: 'user'` through `resolveUserAuthzGrants`) are outside "credentials" and untouched; a maintainer question if the ban is meant to hold the user's actions as well as their credentials.

Prose, sentence by sentence against the diff:
- Changeset title and rule paragraph — true: every key resolution passes the seam; the REST and MCP doors answer the generic 401; a ban with an expiry stops binding on its own (no sign-in needed; the predicate is read-only). "At every door that accepts a key … answered as a key that does not exist" — true on every face whose first statement denies anonymous callers; see ④ item 1 for the one face class where the two answers can differ. "No key row is revoked or rewritten" — true (`stampAdmittedKey` sits below the refusal; pinned). "Who moves" and "The remedy" — true.
- `authentication.mdx` ban-user / unban-user lines — true, subject to the inactivity-window qualification above.
- `administrator-guide.mdx` "Ban / Unban (blocks sign-in, ends the user's sessions, and refuses their API keys while the ban holds)" and the offboarding row — true: the admin ban endpoint deletes the user's sessions as the vendor handler does, and the key refusal is read in the tree.
- Disclosure (`security-findings.md` §2/§6): PR title, body, commits, changeset, docs and both test files stay at rule level — they state what a ban holds and what each door answers, never how a door could be made to misbehave; test names are rules. The ablation paragraph records a mutation and a red count, not an attack. Meets the rule; nothing in the public text needs withdrawing.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing is judged against the published spec on `main` and the cited doors: it makes a refusal the spec already implies (a ban "holds every credential") real at the one seam every key passes, without taking any declared capability away from a consumer whose owner is not banned (controls: peer key served, non-banned owner admitted, cookie-only session unchanged). The ordering is right (a dead key answers for its own state first; the ban before tenancy and posture, so a banned owner's key never reaches the `held` arm or the stamp). Failure modes are the existing ones: an owner read that throws is the branded 503, a store with no `sys_user` table holds no ban, no auth service means no policy but the row's own facts. Timed bans bind until strictly past the expiry and not after, exactly as sign-in; nothing is cached between admissions (the request-grants memo is scoped to one resolution and sits below admission; the stdio transport re-resolves per call). Findings:

1. **Should-fix — guest-serving faces.** On the runtime dispatcher (composed with `anonymous: 'guest'`), an unknown key with no session is served the guest anchor's grants, while a refused key returns before the guest block and is assembled as a guest entry with no grants. Every domain that opens with `shouldDenyAnonymous` answers both the same 401, so the pinned doors hold; but a face that admits a guest for some method/path and then reads the guest's grants answers the two keys differently whenever the guest anchor grants anything — the refused key gets less (fail-closed), yet the difference is observable. This is the same shape the existing org-less refusal already has, so it is not a regression; it is the one place where the PR's "answered as a key that does not exist at every door" is narrower than written. Fix in a follow-up: on the `refused` arm resolve the same guest entry an unknown key resolves, or qualify the claim to anonymous-denying faces.
2. **Should-fix (maintainer question) — absent owner row.** The seam now reads the owner row on every admission and still admits a key whose owner row does not exist. Keeping today's answer is a legitimate scope boundary and the PR says so; it should be an explicit decision rather than an inherited default.
3. **Should-fix — one prose clause.** Changeset and `authentication.mdx`: qualify "admits the same keys again" with the inactivity window (a key idle past the window during a long ban answers as inactive after the unban, remedy a new key), which the PR body already states.
4. Observations, no action: the predicate's flag test is a closed set where the vendor uses truthiness (equivalent for boolean columns; a non-canonical truthy spelling would read as not banned); a refused key's timing class differs from an unknown key's by the owner read and the policy read, as the org-less refusal's already does; `isMissingTableError` recognises a missing table, not an unregistered object — a kernel registering `sys_api_key` without `sys_user` would answer 503 on every key, a composition that does not exist (both ship together in platform-objects) and the same classification `tryFind` already applies.

No must-fix: the rule holds at every door that resolves a key, the refusal is indistinguishable from an unknown key on every door the PR names and on every anonymous-denying face, the key row is untouched, timed bans lapse as sign-in does, and the public text stays at rule level.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set narrowing, the rule — right.** At the one key-admission seam (`resolveApiKeyAdmission`, api-key.ts 753 to 792), after the key's own lifecycle verdict and before the org-less and account-posture questions, the owner row is read by id as the system (`id`, `banned`, `ban_expires`) and a key whose owner's ban holds answers on the `refused` arm (`owner_banned`): no principal, no fall-through to a session sent beside the key, nothing written (`stampAdmittedKey` runs only for an admitted verdict). - **Wire answer per door — right, judged from the cited code.** REST data door (`rest-server.ts` 3412 to 3421, `anonymous: 'fail-closed'`): no principal ⇒ `undefined` context ⇒ `shouldDenyAnonymous` ⇒ `ANONYMOUS_DENY_BODY`, the same bytes an unknown key gets (the dogfood pin compares status, code, message and `WWW-Authenticate` on read and write). Runtime dispatcher and MCP HTTP door (`resolve-execution-context.ts` 199 to 215, `anonymous: 'guest'`; `domains/mcp.ts` 81): a context with no `userId` ⇒ the same 401 for both keys. MCP stdio (`mcp/src/plugin.ts` 258): `resolveAuthzContext` with no guest entry ⇒ no `userId` ⇒ `undefined` at start, re-resolved per call. Storage (`storage-service-plugin.ts` 1566, fail-closed), print, datasource admin routes, sharing and cloud-connection: each calls `resolveAuthzContext` without a guest entry, so a refused key resolves the empty envelope an unknown key resolves. Server side the reason is one `warn` line carrying the row id, the owner id and the reason, never the key or its hash (`warnApiKeyRefusal`, 299 to 312).
- **One anonymous entry (commit 12c342a23d) — right.** `anonymousEntry` (resolve-authz-context.ts 525 to 536) is the one helper both exits call: the `refused` arm (595) and the no-principal branch (649).
